q1: SELECT DISTINCT INSTRUCTOR.ID, INSTRUCTOR.NAME, TEACHES.COURSE_ID FROM INSTRUCTOR LEFT OUTER JOIN TEACHES ON INSTRUCTOR.ID > TEACHES.ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT INSTRUCTOR.ID, INSTRUCTOR.NAME, TEACHES.COURSE_ID FROM INSTRUCTOR, TEACHES WHERE INSTRUCTOR.ID = TEACHES.ID

counterexample: INSERT INTO INSTRUCTOR (ID, NAME, SALARY, DEPT_NAME) VALUES (1, 'John Doe', 50000, 'Math');
explanation: Q1 uses a LEFT OUTER JOIN, which returns all records from the INSTRUCTOR table and the matched records from the TEACHES table. The result is NULL on the side of the TEACHES table, if there is no match. Q2 uses an INNER JOIN, which returns records that have matching values in both tables.
